scope: Isolated AOT cryptography 2.9.0 experiments plus instrumented read/query-only production copy on the private 100k synthetic corpus; actual active 2M database never accessed; concurrent host; no production/dependency changes

sampling.generatedUpperRange: Existing v5 position codec with varied positions in 200-word documents; 900–1000 byte payloads because this stored corpus has no such large posting rows
sampling.timedWork: AES encrypt/decrypt only, excluding SQLite, gzip, fixture generation, RNG and key creation

covers: same AES-256 key, 12-byte nonce, ciphertext and 128-bit tag for all four variants
cached encryption/decryption schedule identity and explicit zeroing on destroy
owning raw key bytes overwritten by owner.destroy
verification.diagnosticOnlyPrivateApi: Expanded schedules were observed using cryptography/src/dart/aes_impl.dart only in the scratch verifier; proposed public integration would not import it

queryAttribution.interpretation: Candidate and numeric passes each read 1666 postings; candidate adds vocabulary/metadata reads. Their AES timings dominate different fractions of each phase. Per-page stopwatch instrumentation adds overhead; values are attribution estimates, not production percentile results.

keyLifecycle.factoryIssue: newSecretKeyFromBytes returns the cached expanded-key subtype but defaults overwriteWhenDestroyed to false. Calling only its destroy wipes expanded schedules but leaves the original caller-owned raw bytes unchanged.
keyLifecycle.verifiedPublicOwnershipRoute: Keep existing SecretKeyData(raw, overwriteWhenDestroyed:true) as owner; cached = await (await DartAesGcm.with256bits().newSecretKeyFromBytes(owner.bytes)).extract(); close cached.destroy() then owner.destroy().
keyLifecycle.recommendation: Do not add this lifecycle state for the measured marginal improvement.

nativeAlternatives.webcrypto: Previously inspected maintained BoringSSL wrapper supports Linux, but imports a private raw-key copy and exposes no public destruction API; exportRawKey returns another copy. It would change explicit cleanup guarantees. Not adopted.
nativeAlternatives.cryptography_flutter: Previously inspected Linux/Windows AES-GCM uses BackgroundAesGcm, still Dart rather than native AES acceleration.
nativeAlternatives.implemented: No FFI, new dependency, GHASH modification, cipher-format change, or authentication weakening.

recommendation: Keep production unchanged. Cache-only gains are generally about 1–3%; combined cached/sync gains are small and variable. Even materially faster AES would leave substantial posting decoding and scoring work; actual 2M measurements remain decisive. The repeated posting decryption between candidate and scoring passes is a concrete reuse opportunity to assess separately.
